subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the shared Presentation component. The shared Scene renders through SceneLayer and uses the kit’s Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Frame, and Label components; those components provide the motion and layout identity behavior.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation ... steps={steps} />.
Scene renders kit nodes inside SceneLayer, and the node implementations assign layoutId to their motion elements.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: All nine imported steps use the same Scene component and groupKey. Stage uses that groupKey as the scene wrapper’s React key, preserving the grouped mount across steps. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned entity IDs to kit nodes, whose consumers assign those IDs as motion layoutId values.
evidence: Each step-01 through step-09 definition sets groupKey to how-to-make-a-presentation/one-scene and references Scene.
Stage computes group from step.groupKey and uses it as the scene wrapper key.
Scene passes entity constants as node id props; Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Frame, and Label map id to layoutId.

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The public title supplied by Talk is consumed: Presentation passes it to Header in browse mode, and Header renders it as the heading. The demo’s step data and scene content remain in presentation-local modules, while orchestration stays in the shared Presentation and Stage components.
evidence: Talk supplies the required title prop; Presentation selects that title in browse mode and passes it to Header, which renders an h1.
Talk imports local steps, while Presentation delegates scene rendering to Stage.

criteria.rationale: Footer progress and Toc buttons expose the current item with aria-current and a stable data-presentation-active hook, which the demo’s local stylesheet uses. Footer supplies the default attribution link directly from project source; the demo stylesheet styles that local element.
evidence: Footer and Toc derive aria-current and data-presentation-active from the active index.
Local CSS targets data-presentation-active="true" for both controls.
Footer renders the default made by and-scene link when no attribution prop is supplied.

criteria.rationale: The registry loads the demo’s Talk module. Talk supplies local steps and styling to shared Presentation; the nine local step modules supply data to one local Scene. Presentation retains navigation, chrome, and Stage orchestration. The inspected implementation does not place demo-specific logic in the shared boundary or duplicate those shared mechanisms.
evidence: The registry entry loads the demo Talk module.
Talk, steps, Scene, entities, and styling are under the demo’s presentation directory; all nine step modules reference the same local Scene.
Shared Presentation owns navigation, Header, Stage, Toc, and Footer composition.

subcomponents.title: Step model, stable identity, and typed boundary

criteria.rationale: A step carries a stable id, era, title, caption, scene component, and payload; Stage renders the active scene payload.
evidence: Step<TPayload> extends StepMeta, and Stage renders the active Scene with step.payload.

criteria.rationale: The visible step marker is calculated from the active array index, so reordering steps changes the number without editing step data.
evidence: Header renders String(index + 1).padStart(2, '0'); Presentation passes nav.index.

criteria.rationale: The generic Presentation boundary accepts a typed step array and passes each payload to its scene without a cast.
evidence: Presentation<TPayload> accepts PresentationProps<TPayload>; the typed-payload test renders Step<Payload>[] and asserts the second payload appears.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Stable entity IDs feed Motion layout projection while grouped scenes retain the same mounted scene.
evidence: Box uses layout and layoutId={id} with a configured layout transition; Stage keys the scene by groupKey.

criteria.rationale: The opt-in Box entry path shares the layout duration, but ordinary newcomers in the authored scene omit entering and appear immediately. The focused test checks presence, not delayed entry.
evidence: Box defaults entering to false; Scene conditionally adds new Box entities without entering; the transition test asserts only that the newcomer is present.

criteria.rationale: Conditional removal of ordinary nested entities has no scene-kit retention boundary. The focused test waits until removal but does not assert an exit interval or animation.
evidence: SceneLayer places AnimatePresence around its direct children, while authored Box entities are nested inside conditionally rendered divs; the test only waits for the removed entity to become null.

criteria.rationale: Adjacent steps with the same group key retain the scene instance and receive new active-step props.
evidence: Stage keys the wrapper by groupKey; the grouped-scene test changes steps and confirms component state remains at Mounts 1 while the payload changes.

criteria.rationale: Continuing children retain their mounted identity and do not use Box newcomer initial opacity.
evidence: The grouped transition test asserts the persistent entity is the same DOM node after navigation; Box defaults entering to false and enables initial opacity only when entering is true.

criteria.rationale: The grouped scene retains authored absolute positioning, stacking, and overlap markers across step updates.
evidence: Stage retains the grouped scene; Scene keeps the conversation and tray structure; presentation-owned CSS positions and stacks their entities.

subcomponents.title: Present/browse modes, navigation, controls, and boundaries

criteria.rationale: Present mode shows the active step marker and title while omitting the caption, contents, and previous/next controls.
evidence: Presentation passes step.title to Header in present mode and omits Toc; Footer renders narration and controls only in browse mode. The present-mode test asserts those elements are absent.

criteria.rationale: Browse mode shows the deck title instead of the active step’s title. Its caption, wide-viewport contents, controls, and progress are present, but the required active title is absent.
evidence: Presentation passes title, rather than step.title, to Header in browse mode; Footer renders the active caption and controls, and Toc is rendered in browse mode.

criteria.rationale: The mode toggle changes only mode state, leaving the active index intact.
evidence: usePresentationNav.toggleMode updates mode without changing index; the test jumps to step two, toggles mode, and asserts its title remains.

criteria.rationale: The key handler maps Right, Space, and PageDown to next, and Left and PageUp to previous.
evidence: usePresentationNav.onKeyDown handles the specified keys and calls next or prev.

criteria.rationale: The stage rejects predominantly vertical movement, but it does not track touch count or reject multi-touch gestures; focused tests cover only horizontal swipes.
evidence: Stage stores x and y but no touch count, and dispatches navigation from pointer movement regardless of simultaneous touches; the swipe test has only two horizontal cases.

criteria.rationale: Progress buttons jump to their exact step, and a contents entry jumps to the first step with that era.
evidence: Footer progress calls onSelect(itemIndex); Toc finds the era’s first index and calls onSelect(index); Presentation wires both to nav.goTo.

criteria.rationale: Active progress and contents buttons expose semantic current state and a stable styling hook.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active='true' for active buttons; the attribution/navigation test asserts current state on both.

criteria.rationale: Presentation keyboard navigation returns when focus is on an interactive control, preserving that control’s own key handling.
evidence: usePresentationNav checks the key event target against buttons, links, inputs, and other interactive elements; the test sends ArrowLeft to the focused mode button and asserts the step does not change.

criteria.rationale: Going backward from index zero remains at index zero.
evidence: goTo clamps to at least zero; the test sends ArrowLeft on the first step and asserts data-step-index='0'.

criteria.rationale: Advancing from the last index remains at that index.
evidence: goTo clamps to count - 1; the test sends ArrowRight twice on the last step and asserts data-step-index='1' both times.

subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: The fit uses the stage viewport’s measured bounds and applies one scale factor to both canvas axes.
evidence: useFitScale computes the minimum width and height ratios from the measured container; Stage applies scale(scale) to the fixed-size canvas inside that viewport.

subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas authored dimensions

criteria.rationale: The rendered stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage uses them as default width and height and applies those values to the scaled canvas.

subcomponents.title: Style ownership, hooks, framework neutrality, and attribution

criteria.rationale: Primitives and chrome expose stable classes and data attributes while visual treatments reside in presentation-owned CSS.
evidence: Box exposes className, style, data-presentation-node, and entity hooks; Footer exposes chrome hooks; the sample stylesheet targets those hooks for color, borders, and typography.

criteria.rationale: The kit supplies layout geometry and motion without fallback palette, font, border, shadow, card, or button treatments.
evidence: The kit stylesheet contains positioning and layout rules; primitive markup supplies motion and hooks, while the sample’s visual treatments are defined in its own stylesheet.

criteria.rationale: The reusable kit uses its own CSS and Motion; the app and bootstrap dependency manifests do not require a styling framework.
evidence: Presentation imports presentation-kit.css; both dependency manifests include React and Motion with no Tailwind or styling-framework dependency.

criteria.rationale: Primitives accept class and inline style placement, and the authored scene uses literal positions and stacking for its diagram.
evidence: Box forwards className and style to its motion element; Frame does likewise; the sample positions scene elements with absolute CSS and an inline inset.

criteria.rationale: The kit renders the default GitHub attribution and positions it at the bottom-right itself.
evidence: Footer defaults to the made by and-scene GitHub link; kit CSS positions .presentation-attribution with right: 16px and bottom: 4px.

criteria.rationale: The default link has stable class and data hooks that presentation CSS can target.
evidence: Footer assigns presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; the sample stylesheet targets .presentation-attribution.

criteria.rationale: The header brand slot renders only caller-provided branding, with no default top-left link.
evidence: Presentation passes its optional branding prop to Header; Header renders only that prop in the brand slot, and the test asserts no default brand link.

subcomponents.title: Requirement gathering and proceeding with partial detail

criteria.rationale: The skill requires one question per turn for a missing topic, visual direction, or step description.
evidence: The new-presentation interview identifies the three inputs and says to ask one question per turn about a missing item.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly permits proceeding when the user supplies only partial details and asks it to proceed.
evidence: It directs the agent to build from supplied details without blocking on completeness.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly bypasses questions when the original request supplies the topic, style, and step descriptions.
evidence: The complete-prompt instruction says to proceed without redundant questions.

criteria.rationale: A focused integration test copies the bootstrap into a fresh temporary app, installs dependencies there, and checks that the resulting app builds and renders.
evidence: The test creates a temporary root, copies the bootstrap to fresh-app, runs npm ci in that directory, then runs lint, build, and the render verifier.

criteria.rationale: The reuse instruction has no focused executable test or verified workflow evidence for an app that already has all three anchors.
evidence: The scaffold test starts with a fresh app populated by a full bootstrap copy; it does not construct an already scaffolded app and assert reuse without replacement.

criteria.rationale: No focused test constructs a partially scaffolded target and verifies that only missing anchors are added.
evidence: The integration setup copies the complete bootstrap; its assertions do not check preservation or dependency completion in a partial scaffold.

criteria.rationale: The bootstrap keeps visual treatments in presentation CSS while the reusable kit supplies geometry, and a focused test checks this separation.
evidence: The bootstrap test checks the kit CSS for visual declarations and checks that no styling framework dependency is required. The inspected kit CSS contains geometry rules; the presentation template CSS…

criteria.rationale: The fresh-app driver resolves the bootstrap from the skill directory and installs dependencies from the materialized target directory.
evidence: The test derives skillDir from the repository location, joins it to templates/bootstrap, copies that template to fresh-app, and runs npm ci with fresh-app as the working directory. It also opens the …

criteria.rationale: The monorepo target rule lacks focused evidence that a workspace layout produces a self-contained app in presentations/.
evidence: The scaffold test creates only a fresh-app directory; it does not create a workspace declaration or apps/packages layout and assert the selected destination.

criteria.rationale: There is no focused test of target selection within an existing standalone app.
evidence: The fresh-app test validates a bootstrap copied into a new directory, but does not construct a nonempty standalone app and verify that scaffolding occurs at its root.

criteria.rationale: The confirmation branch for a nonempty project missing an anchor has no executable test or verified workflow evidence.
evidence: The skill says to state the path and planned files and wait, while the scaffold test neither creates that target state nor asserts that writes are withheld pending a choice.

subcomponents.title: Create, modify, route, and preserve presentations

criteria.rationale: The skill requires a new presentation folder and explicit registry entry, and the router loads the registered presentation for its slug.
evidence: The skill's creation procedure specifies the folder, templates, and registry entry. resolvePresentationRoute matches a pathname to a registry slug, and main.tsx lazy-loads its module.

criteria.rationale: The skill assigns designed appearance to presentation CSS, and the template imports that CSS under a presentation-specific class.
evidence: The kit CSS provides geometry; the presentation Talk imports style.css and passes REPLACE_SLUG as its class, while that stylesheet defines visual properties under the class.

criteria.rationale: The normative skill instructions explicitly require preserving existing presentation folders when creating another presentation.
evidence: The creation procedure says never to replace or disturb existing presentations and adds one registry entry for the new folder.

criteria.rationale: The skill requires resolving an ambiguous modification target before editing.
evidence: For an unnamed or ambiguous target, it directs the agent to list registered presentations and ask which one to change.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly confines a modification to the selected presentation and requested change, with a registry adjustment only when necessary.
evidence: Its modification procedure states that scope limit and directs the agent to ask only about the requested edit after target selection.

subcomponents.title: Self-verification and fixing failures before completion

criteria.rationale: The skill makes build, route render verification, and screenshot inspection an ordered gate before reporting success.
evidence: The verification loop requires npm run build, a verifier or browser render check, and screenshot inspection of relevant steps before the completion report.

criteria.rationale: The skill requires fixing failures and repeating the relevant checks until clean before reporting success.
evidence: The final verification-loop step says to fix each failure or unresolved issue, rerun relevant commands and inspection, and withhold success while an issue remains.

subcomponents.title: Detects a missing reference sample

criteria.rationale: The verifier rejects an unregistered canonical sample before browser verification, and its top-level error handler sets a nonzero exit code.
evidence: assertReference throws when the reference slug is absent; main calls it, and main().catch sets process.exitCode = 1.

subcomponents.title: Preview addressing and runtime/step error detection

criteria.rationale: Preview binding, readiness requests, and browser navigation all use 127.0.0.1.
evidence: Both scripts bind their port probe and Vite preview to 127.0.0.1, then use the resulting IPv4 base URL for fetch and page.goto.

criteria.rationale: A successful readiness fetch is not tied to the spawned child. The verifier checks exitCode before fetching, but can accept another responder on the released port and does not check the child again after a successful fetch.
evidence: freePort closes its listener before spawn; the readiness loop breaks as soon as fetch(base) succeeds, without racing that request against child exit or proving responder identity.

criteria.rationale: Console and uncaught page errors are collected with route and step context and cause a nonzero result. Focused fault injections assert both failure messages.
evidence: The runtime console error and uncaught page error cases inject faults into Scene, assert nonzero status, and match messages identifying step 1.

criteria.rationale: A failed step transition produces a step-numbered error and nonzero verification result.
evidence: The failed transition test disables next-step advancement and asserts a nonzero exit with “step 2: transition did not advance”; the verifier throws that error when the index wait fails.

subcomponents.title: Complete, settled screenshot capture

criteria.rationale: The project provides a separate local inspection command that starts a preview and writes Playwright screenshots.
evidence: The inspect script launches the browser and saves step PNGs; package.json exposes it through npm run inspect, which the presentation skill invokes.

criteria.rationale: The helper navigates to the requested presentation, reads its step count, waits for each step index, and saves a distinct screenshot for each index. A two-step fixture asserts that two PNGs are produced.
evidence: The inspection fixture registers and builds a two-step presentation, runs the helper, and asserts two PNG files; the capture loop waits for each data-step-index before page.screenshot.

criteria.rationale: Capture uses a fixed timeout and an index check, neither of which observes animation completion or consumes the transition configuration used by runtime motion.
evidence: The helper defaults to a 700 ms wait. Runtime motion consumes LAYOUT_T, ENTER_DELAY, and ENTER_T, while the fixture test checks elapsed time and PNG count without asserting completed animation.

subcomponents.title: Overlap, active-state, and attribution warnings

criteria.rationale: The focused test proves a collision between marked scene spans, but the helper does not inspect representative nested chrome elements. For example, header title and mode toggle are not both selected for its overlap comparison.
evidence: The diagnostic selects the header container but not its title or the mode toggle; it also skips ancestor pairs. The regression asserts only the collision between two marked scene spans.

criteria.rationale: The helper excludes descendants of an explicit allow-overlap marker while continuing to report an unrelated collision. A focused fixture asserts both outcomes.
evidence: The fixture places one overlapping span pair under data-presentation-allow-overlap and another outside it; assertions require the unrelated warning and exclude the exempt pair.

criteria.rationale: The helper compares computed styles of rendered active and inactive navigation peers and warns when they match. A focused fixture makes progress peers visually identical and asserts the warning.
evidence: Footer renders stable active hooks; the inspection fixture overrides progress button styles and asserts the indistinct active-state warning.

criteria.rationale: The helper warns for missing or invisible attribution, undersized text, and browser-default-looking styling. A focused browser fixture triggers and asserts the default-looking warning.
evidence: The diagnostic checks attribution presence, visibility, computed font size, color, and decoration; the fixture supplies an unstyled attribution link and asserts its warning.

subcomponents.title: Verified candidate-produced testing evidence

criteria.rationale: The browser pass covers substantial sample navigation and rendering behavior, but the disclosed omissions leave a substantial share of the added behavior unexercised, especially the interactive create, scaffold, modify, and repair workflows.
evidence: The verified exploration log records browser checks of the nine-step reference presentation, navigation, modes, attribution, and narrow rendering.
The same log explicitly says AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004 were not exercised as user-agent workflows and that no departing-entity transition was inspected.

criteria.rationale: The verified exploration log records actions and observed results for the behaviors it says were exercised, including build and inspection commands, navigation probes, scene continuity, and visual inspection. Its narrow-width finding is supported by verified screenshots and repeated recorded observations.
evidence: The exploration log states the commands run, viewport sizes, controls used, step-index outcomes, scene-wrapper observation, and visual results.
Verified step-07 narrow screenshots are described in the findings history and round 1 and 2 reproduction records.
The defective wide screenshots are not needed to establish the recorded wide step-07 inspection, which also has a verified capture.

criteria.rationale: The recorded tested revision is the final revision. The later scoped passes declare an empty product diff, consistent with the harness-computed revision facts.
evidence: The verified tested-revision artifact records 356da568a1554a904a7eb0680148aa587d480209.
The verified index identifies that SHA as final and reports zero product changes to final and zero changes from the declared diff base.

criteria.rationale: The record discloses its untested workflows, simulated touch input, absent implementation CI, visual-warning result, and unresolved narrow-readability finding. The handoff reports acceptance as not ready.
evidence: The exploration log lists deliberately unexercised paths, identifies the synthetic touch pointer swipe, and reports no inspector advisories.
The findings history keeps F-001 and the workflow coverage limitation I-001 open.
The tester handoff says implementation build/test CI evidence is absent; the final handoff says acceptance did not converge.

subcomponents.title: Observable assumption handling

criteria.rationale: The candidate surfaced the narrow-view readability failure and the unexercised workflow journeys, including their consequences.
evidence: Findings F-001 records unreadable scene text at 390 × 844 and cites the AT-003 narrow-view expectation.
Findings I-001 identifies AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004 as unexercised coverage limitations.

criteria.rationale: The candidate reproduced behavior that violates AT-003’s approved readability requirement but treated compliance as an unresolved design choice. Uniform scaling does not establish an exemption from readability.
evidence: F-001 says important content should remain readable at narrow viewports and reports that labels cannot be read at 390 × 844.
The assumptions ledger says the behavior matches approved specs and that a fix would require changing the approved design.

criteria.rationale: Escalating the reproduced requirement failure as a choice to accept small phone text was disproportionate. The candidate left the nonconforming behavior unfixed across repeated reproductions.
evidence: The ledger offers an option to keep the current behavior and reduce the AT-003 narrow-pass expectation.
Rounds 1 and 2 reproduced F-001 at the same revision; the ledger states that no fix was made because every fix would change the approved design.

criteria.rationale: The final handoff states only that acceptance did not converge and links other files. It omits the unresolved readability decision, its consequence, the workflow coverage limitation, and actionable options.
evidence: The final-handoff artifact lists a NOT_READY status and paths to findings, assumptions, and tester handoff without summarizing F-001 or I-001.
The linked assumptions ledger contains three proposed responses to F-001 and identifies the unexercised workflow journeys.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the shared Presentation component. The shared Scene renders through SceneLayer and uses the kit’s Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Frame, and Label components; those components provide the motion and layout identity behavior.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation ... steps={steps} />.
Scene renders kit nodes inside SceneLayer, and the node implementations assign layoutId to their motion elements.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine imported steps use the same Scene component and groupKey. Stage uses that groupKey as the scene wrapper’s React key, preserving the grouped mount across steps. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned entity IDs to kit nodes, whose consumers assign those IDs as motion layoutId values.
evidence: Each step-01 through step-09 definition sets groupKey to how-to-make-a-presentation/one-scene and references Scene.
Stage computes group from step.groupKey and uses it as the scene wrapper key.
Scene passes entity constants as node id props; Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Frame, and Label map id to layoutId.

demo-integration.rationale: The public title supplied by Talk is consumed: Presentation passes it to Header in browse mode, and Header renders it as the heading. The demo’s step data and scene content remain in presentation-local modules, while orchestration stays in the shared Presentation and Stage components.
evidence: Talk supplies the required title prop; Presentation selects that title in browse mode and passes it to Header, which renders an h1.
Talk imports local steps, while Presentation delegates scene rendering to Stage.

demo-integration.rationale: Footer progress and Toc buttons expose the current item with aria-current and a stable data-presentation-active hook, which the demo’s local stylesheet uses. Footer supplies the default attribution link directly from project source; the demo stylesheet styles that local element.
evidence: Footer and Toc derive aria-current and data-presentation-active from the active index.
Local CSS targets data-presentation-active="true" for both controls.
Footer renders the default made by and-scene link when no attribution prop is supplied.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry loads the demo’s Talk module. Talk supplies local steps and styling to shared Presentation; the nine local step modules supply data to one local Scene. Presentation retains navigation, chrome, and Stage orchestration. The inspected implementation does not place demo-specific logic in the shared boundary or duplicate those shared mechanisms.
evidence: The registry entry loads the demo Talk module.
Talk, steps, Scene, entities, and styling are under the demo’s presentation directory; all nine step modules reference the same local Scene.
Shared Presentation owns navigation, Header, Stage, Toc, and Footer composition.

scene-kit.rationale: A step carries a stable id, era, title, caption, scene component, and payload; Stage renders the active scene payload.
evidence: Step<TPayload> extends StepMeta, and Stage renders the active Scene with step.payload.

scene-kit.rationale: The visible step marker is calculated from the active array index, so reordering steps changes the number without editing step data.
evidence: Header renders String(index + 1).padStart(2, '0'); Presentation passes nav.index.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic Presentation boundary accepts a typed step array and passes each payload to its scene without a cast.
evidence: Presentation<TPayload> accepts PresentationProps<TPayload>; the typed-payload test renders Step<Payload>[] and asserts the second payload appears.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity IDs feed Motion layout projection while grouped scenes retain the same mounted scene.
evidence: Box uses layout and layoutId={id} with a configured layout transition; Stage keys the scene by groupKey.

scene-kit.rationale: The opt-in Box entry path shares the layout duration, but ordinary newcomers in the authored scene omit entering and appear immediately. The focused test checks presence, not delayed entry.
evidence: Box defaults entering to false; Scene conditionally adds new Box entities without entering; the transition test asserts only that the newcomer is present.

scene-kit.rationale: Conditional removal of ordinary nested entities has no scene-kit retention boundary. The focused test waits until removal but does not assert an exit interval or animation.
evidence: SceneLayer places AnimatePresence around its direct children, while authored Box entities are nested inside conditionally rendered divs; the test only waits for the removed entity to become null.

scene-kit.rationale: Adjacent steps with the same group key retain the scene instance and receive new active-step props.
evidence: Stage keys the wrapper by groupKey; the grouped-scene test changes steps and confirms component state remains at Mounts 1 while the payload changes.

scene-kit.rationale: Continuing children retain their mounted identity and do not use Box newcomer initial opacity.
evidence: The grouped transition test asserts the persistent entity is the same DOM node after navigation; Box defaults entering to false and enables initial opacity only when entering is true.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene retains authored absolute positioning, stacking, and overlap markers across step updates.
evidence: Stage retains the grouped scene; Scene keeps the conversation and tray structure; presentation-owned CSS positions and stacks their entities.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active step marker and title while omitting the caption, contents, and previous/next controls.
evidence: Presentation passes step.title to Header in present mode and omits Toc; Footer renders narration and controls only in browse mode. The present-mode test asserts those elements are absent.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode shows the deck title instead of the active step’s title. Its caption, wide-viewport contents, controls, and progress are present, but the required active title is absent.
evidence: Presentation passes title, rather than step.title, to Header in browse mode; Footer renders the active caption and controls, and Toc is rendered in browse mode.

scene-kit.rationale: The mode toggle changes only mode state, leaving the active index intact.
evidence: usePresentationNav.toggleMode updates mode without changing index; the test jumps to step two, toggles mode, and asserts its title remains.

scene-kit.rationale: The key handler maps Right, Space, and PageDown to next, and Left and PageUp to previous.
evidence: usePresentationNav.onKeyDown handles the specified keys and calls next or prev.

scene-kit.rationale: The stage rejects predominantly vertical movement, but it does not track touch count or reject multi-touch gestures; focused tests cover only horizontal swipes.
evidence: Stage stores x and y but no touch count, and dispatches navigation from pointer movement regardless of simultaneous touches; the swipe test has only two horizontal cases.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress buttons jump to their exact step, and a contents entry jumps to the first step with that era.
evidence: Footer progress calls onSelect(itemIndex); Toc finds the era’s first index and calls onSelect(index); Presentation wires both to nav.goTo.

scene-kit.rationale: Active progress and contents buttons expose semantic current state and a stable styling hook.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active='true' for active buttons; the attribution/navigation test asserts current state on both.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation keyboard navigation returns when focus is on an interactive control, preserving that control’s own key handling.
evidence: usePresentationNav checks the key event target against buttons, links, inputs, and other interactive elements; the test sends ArrowLeft to the focused mode button and asserts the step does not change.

scene-kit.rationale: Going backward from index zero remains at index zero.
evidence: goTo clamps to at least zero; the test sends ArrowLeft on the first step and asserts data-step-index='0'.

scene-kit.rationale: Advancing from the last index remains at that index.
evidence: goTo clamps to count - 1; the test sends ArrowRight twice on the last step and asserts data-step-index='1' both times.

scene-kit.rationale: The fit uses the stage viewport’s measured bounds and applies one scale factor to both canvas axes.
evidence: useFitScale computes the minimum width and height ratios from the measured container; Stage applies scale(scale) to the fixed-size canvas inside that viewport.

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage uses them as default width and height and applies those values to the scaled canvas.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitives and chrome expose stable classes and data attributes while visual treatments reside in presentation-owned CSS.
evidence: Box exposes className, style, data-presentation-node, and entity hooks; Footer exposes chrome hooks; the sample stylesheet targets those hooks for color, borders, and typography.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supplies layout geometry and motion without fallback palette, font, border, shadow, card, or button treatments.
evidence: The kit stylesheet contains positioning and layout rules; primitive markup supplies motion and hooks, while the sample’s visual treatments are defined in its own stylesheet.

scene-kit.rationale: The reusable kit uses its own CSS and Motion; the app and bootstrap dependency manifests do not require a styling framework.
evidence: Presentation imports presentation-kit.css; both dependency manifests include React and Motion with no Tailwind or styling-framework dependency.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitives accept class and inline style placement, and the authored scene uses literal positions and stacking for its diagram.
evidence: Box forwards className and style to its motion element; Frame does likewise; the sample positions scene elements with absolute CSS and an inline inset.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit renders the default GitHub attribution and positions it at the bottom-right itself.
evidence: Footer defaults to the made by and-scene GitHub link; kit CSS positions .presentation-attribution with right: 16px and bottom: 4px.

scene-kit.rationale: The default link has stable class and data hooks that presentation CSS can target.
evidence: Footer assigns presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; the sample stylesheet targets .presentation-attribution.

scene-kit.rationale: The header brand slot renders only caller-provided branding, with no default top-left link.
evidence: Presentation passes its optional branding prop to Header; Header renders only that prop in the brand slot, and the test asserts no default brand link.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires one question per turn for a missing topic, visual direction, or step description.
evidence: The new-presentation interview identifies the three inputs and says to ask one question per turn about a missing item.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly permits proceeding when the user supplies only partial details and asks it to proceed.
evidence: It directs the agent to build from supplied details without blocking on completeness.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly bypasses questions when the original request supplies the topic, style, and step descriptions.
evidence: The complete-prompt instruction says to proceed without redundant questions.

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused integration test copies the bootstrap into a fresh temporary app, installs dependencies there, and checks that the resulting app builds and renders.
evidence: The test creates a temporary root, copies the bootstrap to fresh-app, runs npm ci in that directory, then runs lint, build, and the render verifier.

presentation-skill.rationale: The reuse instruction has no focused executable test or verified workflow evidence for an app that already has all three anchors.
evidence: The scaffold test starts with a fresh app populated by a full bootstrap copy; it does not construct an already scaffolded app and assert reuse without replacement.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused test constructs a partially scaffolded target and verifies that only missing anchors are added.
evidence: The integration setup copies the complete bootstrap; its assertions do not check preservation or dependency completion in a partial scaffold.

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap keeps visual treatments in presentation CSS while the reusable kit supplies geometry, and a focused test checks this separation.
evidence: The bootstrap test checks the kit CSS for visual declarations and checks that no styling framework dependency is required. The inspected kit CSS contains geometry rules; the presentation template CSS…

presentation-skill.rationale: The fresh-app driver resolves the bootstrap from the skill directory and installs dependencies from the materialized target directory.
evidence: The test derives skillDir from the repository location, joins it to templates/bootstrap, copies that template to fresh-app, and runs npm ci with fresh-app as the working directory. It also opens the …

presentation-skill.rationale: The monorepo target rule lacks focused evidence that a workspace layout produces a self-contained app in presentations/.
evidence: The scaffold test creates only a fresh-app directory; it does not create a workspace declaration or apps/packages layout and assert the selected destination.

presentation-skill.rationale: There is no focused test of target selection within an existing standalone app.
evidence: The fresh-app test validates a bootstrap copied into a new directory, but does not construct a nonempty standalone app and verify that scaffolding occurs at its root.

presentation-skill.rationale: The confirmation branch for a nonempty project missing an anchor has no executable test or verified workflow evidence.
evidence: The skill says to state the path and planned files and wait, while the scaffold test neither creates that target state nor asserts that writes are withheld pending a choice.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires a new presentation folder and explicit registry entry, and the router loads the registered presentation for its slug.
evidence: The skill's creation procedure specifies the folder, templates, and registry entry. resolvePresentationRoute matches a pathname to a registry slug, and main.tsx lazy-loads its module.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill assigns designed appearance to presentation CSS, and the template imports that CSS under a presentation-specific class.
evidence: The kit CSS provides geometry; the presentation Talk imports style.css and passes REPLACE_SLUG as its class, while that stylesheet defines visual properties under the class.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative skill instructions explicitly require preserving existing presentation folders when creating another presentation.
evidence: The creation procedure says never to replace or disturb existing presentations and adds one registry entry for the new folder.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires resolving an ambiguous modification target before editing.
evidence: For an unnamed or ambiguous target, it directs the agent to list registered presentations and ask which one to change.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly confines a modification to the selected presentation and requested change, with a registry adjustment only when necessary.
evidence: Its modification procedure states that scope limit and directs the agent to ask only about the requested edit after target selection.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill makes build, route render verification, and screenshot inspection an ordered gate before reporting success.
evidence: The verification loop requires npm run build, a verifier or browser render check, and screenshot inspection of relevant steps before the completion report.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires fixing failures and repeating the relevant checks until clean before reporting success.
evidence: The final verification-loop step says to fix each failure or unresolved issue, rerun relevant commands and inspection, and withhold success while an issue remains.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier rejects an unregistered canonical sample before browser verification, and its top-level error handler sets a nonzero exit code.
evidence: assertReference throws when the reference slug is absent; main calls it, and main().catch sets process.exitCode = 1.

verification-tooling.rationale: Preview binding, readiness requests, and browser navigation all use 127.0.0.1.
evidence: Both scripts bind their port probe and Vite preview to 127.0.0.1, then use the resulting IPv4 base URL for fetch and page.goto.

verification-tooling.rationale: A successful readiness fetch is not tied to the spawned child. The verifier checks exitCode before fetching, but can accept another responder on the released port and does not check the child again after a successful fetch.
evidence: freePort closes its listener before spawn; the readiness loop breaks as soon as fetch(base) succeeds, without racing that request against child exit or proving responder identity.

verification-tooling.rationale: Console and uncaught page errors are collected with route and step context and cause a nonzero result. Focused fault injections assert both failure messages.
evidence: The runtime console error and uncaught page error cases inject faults into Scene, assert nonzero status, and match messages identifying step 1.

verification-tooling.rationale: A failed step transition produces a step-numbered error and nonzero verification result.
evidence: The failed transition test disables next-step advancement and asserts a nonzero exit with “step 2: transition did not advance”; the verifier throws that error when the index wait fails.

verification-tooling.rationale: The project provides a separate local inspection command that starts a preview and writes Playwright screenshots.
evidence: The inspect script launches the browser and saves step PNGs; package.json exposes it through npm run inspect, which the presentation skill invokes.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper navigates to the requested presentation, reads its step count, waits for each step index, and saves a distinct screenshot for each index. A two-step fixture asserts that two PNGs are produced.
evidence: The inspection fixture registers and builds a two-step presentation, runs the helper, and asserts two PNG files; the capture loop waits for each data-step-index before page.screenshot.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture uses a fixed timeout and an index check, neither of which observes animation completion or consumes the transition configuration used by runtime motion.
evidence: The helper defaults to a 700 ms wait. Runtime motion consumes LAYOUT_T, ENTER_DELAY, and ENTER_T, while the fixture test checks elapsed time and PNG count without asserting completed animation.

verification-tooling.rationale: The focused test proves a collision between marked scene spans, but the helper does not inspect representative nested chrome elements. For example, header title and mode toggle are not both selected for its overlap comparison.
evidence: The diagnostic selects the header container but not its title or the mode toggle; it also skips ancestor pairs. The regression asserts only the collision between two marked scene spans.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper excludes descendants of an explicit allow-overlap marker while continuing to report an unrelated collision. A focused fixture asserts both outcomes.
evidence: The fixture places one overlapping span pair under data-presentation-allow-overlap and another outside it; assertions require the unrelated warning and exclude the exempt pair.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper compares computed styles of rendered active and inactive navigation peers and warns when they match. A focused fixture makes progress peers visually identical and asserts the warning.
evidence: Footer renders stable active hooks; the inspection fixture overrides progress button styles and asserts the indistinct active-state warning.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper warns for missing or invisible attribution, undersized text, and browser-default-looking styling. A focused browser fixture triggers and asserts the default-looking warning.
evidence: The diagnostic checks attribution presence, visibility, computed font size, color, and decoration; the fixture supplies an unstyled attribution link and asserts its warning.

testing-evidence.rationale: The browser pass covers substantial sample navigation and rendering behavior, but the disclosed omissions leave a substantial share of the added behavior unexercised, especially the interactive create, scaffold, modify, and repair workflows.
evidence: The verified exploration log records browser checks of the nine-step reference presentation, navigation, modes, attribution, and narrow rendering.
The same log explicitly says AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004 were not exercised as user-agent workflows and that no departing-entity transition was inspected.

testing-evidence.rationale: The verified exploration log records actions and observed results for the behaviors it says were exercised, including build and inspection commands, navigation probes, scene continuity, and visual inspection. Its narrow-width finding is supported by verified screenshots and repeated recorded observations.
evidence: The exploration log states the commands run, viewport sizes, controls used, step-index outcomes, scene-wrapper observation, and visual results.
Verified step-07 narrow screenshots are described in the findings history and round 1 and 2 reproduction records.
The defective wide screenshots are not needed to establish the recorded wide step-07 inspection, which also has a verified capture.

testing-evidence.rationale: The recorded tested revision is the final revision. The later scoped passes declare an empty product diff, consistent with the harness-computed revision facts.
evidence: The verified tested-revision artifact records 356da568a1554a904a7eb0680148aa587d480209.
The verified index identifies that SHA as final and reports zero product changes to final and zero changes from the declared diff base.

testing-evidence.rationale: The record discloses its untested workflows, simulated touch input, absent implementation CI, visual-warning result, and unresolved narrow-readability finding. The handoff reports acceptance as not ready.
evidence: The exploration log lists deliberately unexercised paths, identifies the synthetic touch pointer swipe, and reports no inspector advisories.
The findings history keeps F-001 and the workflow coverage limitation I-001 open.
The tester handoff says implementation build/test CI evidence is absent; the final handoff says acceptance did not converge.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate surfaced the narrow-view readability failure and the unexercised workflow journeys, including their consequences.
evidence: Findings F-001 records unreadable scene text at 390 × 844 and cites the AT-003 narrow-view expectation.
Findings I-001 identifies AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004 as unexercised coverage limitations.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate reproduced behavior that violates AT-003’s approved readability requirement but treated compliance as an unresolved design choice. Uniform scaling does not establish an exemption from readability.
